Subject: Recap: model fit & multilingual QA (EU + APAC) — next steps

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

TL;DR
- Goal: production-grade NLU + structured output for customer support routing and KYC automation across EU (IT/ES/FR/DE) and APAC (JA/KO/ZH-CN).
- Constraints: GDPR data residency for EU datasets, target 95th pct latency < 200ms for short form responses, token-cost sensitivity for high throughput flows.

What we heard (from the call)
- Elena: priority languages are Italian + Spanish + French; German later. GDPR residency and audit logs are checkboxes.
- Kenji: APAC pilot will focus on Japanese first; character/tokenization quirks and politeness nuances are important.

Recommended immediate plan (proposed)
1) Redwood to run a small scoped eval (2 weeks) across recommended model variants on a shared prompt set (attached: locale_prompt_sets_v1.csv).
2) Metrics: quality pass = 90% intent classification accuracy / 0.8 F1 on entity extraction / human-rated fluency >= 4.2 out of 5. Include per-locale baselines.
3) Model candidates: RW-3.1-multilang (float16 baseline), RW-3.1-multilang-quant (int8 / int4 candidate), and a smaller low-cost fallback RW-2.7-small for cheap throughput.
4) Deliverables: benchmark report, per-locale prompt tuning notes, prompt-set tweaks for vendor/localization team, and recommended rollout plan including canary thresholds.

Dependencies we need from you
- Elena: share a small set of representative utterances (anonymized) and desired intents/labels (csv) — or confirm we can use the sample in the attachment.
- Kenji: confirm acceptance to include LinguaEdge in prompt tuning (Anita copied here).

Attachments included: locale_prompt_sets_v1.csv (seed prompts), evaluation_plan_brief.pdf (summary).

Proposed timeline
- Confirm scope & demo data by 2026-05-22
- Redwood runs evals: 2026-05-23 — 2026-06-04
- Review call with findings: week of 2026-06-07

If that looks good I will kick off the eval job and loop in Maya (ML eval lead) to run the tests.

Thanks,

Subject: Results & recommended models — FinTech EU multilingual eval (initial)

Hi all — quick initial results and recommendations from the scoped eval (see attached benchmark PDF for full tables). Summary:  

Findings
- RW-3.1-multilang (fp16 baseline) achieved the best quality across EU languages: Italian/Spanish/French per-intent accuracy 91–94%, entity F1 0.82–0.86, human fluency ~4.4. Minor diacritic tokenization gaps observed for French NER spans (~1.5% span bias).
- RW-3.1-multilang-quant (int8) shows a small regression in French diacritics and Japanese polite-form generation vs fp16 baseline (delta: -2–3% in F1). Latency improved ~18% and token cost reduced ~32%.
- RW-2.7-small is a reasonable cost-saving fallback for bulk non-critical routing but fails our 90% intent threshold on Italian (avg 87%).

Recommendations
1) Phase 1: deploy RW-3.1-multilang (fp16) for EU core flows to meet accuracy SLA. Use RW-3.1-multilang-quant for a canary on low-risk flows where lower cost is essential; measure per-locale regression and abort if per-locale F1 drops >2.5%.
2) For Japanese: use RW-3.1-multilang (fp16) with LinguaEdge prompt tuning. Quantization requires additional locale-specific QA (we observed polite-form regressions).
3) Prompt tweaks: small token-preserving changes for French diacritics (see prompt_set "FR_fix_tokens" in attached CSV).

Deliverables included
- eu_apac_benchmarks_v1.pdf (detailed tables, per-locale confusion matrices, latency/cost tradeoffs)
- locale_prompt_sets_v1.csv (seed prompts + FR_fix_tokens + JP_politeness variants)
- short playbook: canary thresholds and rollback steps (in PDF appendix).

Risks and next steps
- Quality regression risk with quantized variants — we recommend an A/B with human-in-the-loop checks for the first 5k requests in-circuit before full promote.
- For GDPR/residency: ensure logs and any retained cache blobs are pinned to eu-west-1; Neha please confirm config.

I'll schedule a short walkthrough of the benchmark doc on the review call. If the customer signs off, ops can prepare canary config and we can ship a small test fleet.
